content.comment_body: Hello, I am currently working with [product_name] and the [product_name] to develop a production counting system that provides operators with real-time data. I've encountered some issues regarding the data logging. Although I set the system to log data every 60 seconds, the interval seems to increase slightly each time the counters are reset. Additionally, the time stamping is problematic: my setup resets counters at specific times (on the hour, 15 minutes past, 30 minutes past, and 15 minutes before the hour), but the logs sometimes record up to two minutes late, which disrupts my spreadsheet calculations. I tried syncing the time between the device and the PC, but the issue persists. Would using an NTP server with GPS capabilities potentially resolve these timing discrepancies? Thanks.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is encountering timing and time-stamping issues with data logging using [product_name] and [product_name], resulting in discrepancies when analyzing the logs in a spreadsheet. Even after synchronizing clocks between the PC and the device, irregularities persist, leading the user to consider an NTP GPS solution for improved accuracy.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects precise, scheduled data logging and accurate, synchronized time stamps between the device and the PC, with no drift after counter resets, to support efficient spreadsheet analysis.
